biggestGap: Shade the LARGEST mass of every sprite, not the smallest. Measured: FFVI's own monster in reference/shots/ffvi-battle-native-a.png puts a 10-value ramp on its biggest colour mass (1534px) and a 3-value ramp on its second (1175px). Our slagmaw.png inverts this -- its 2nd, 3rd and 4th largest masses (501px #100810, 474px #181820, 324px) carry ramp depths of 1, 1 and 2, so 29% of the sprite is painted in single flat values. tessin-idle.png is worse: its single largest region (73px of 223, a third of the whole sprite) is one flat #081018, which is why the mage reads on screen as a purple domino rather than a robed figure. The colour budget is not the constraint -- these sprites average 14 of an allowed 16 colours, but spend them on local colour (a hue per garment) instead of on value ramps. Re-author every hero and monster so each material carries 3-4 values from one consistent light direction, weighting ramp depth toward pixel area, and the sprite half will match the engineering half.
evidence: CRITIC VERDICT, judged from pixels. Replaces the builder self-assessment that previously occupied this file (which scored itself 74). Inspected: battle.html and atelier.html at 390x844 via tools/shot.mjs at DPR 2 and DPR 3; live DOM geometry over CDP in a real Chrome; all 33 atelier PNGs decoded with an independently written zlib/PNG decoder rather than the project's own audit tool; blind A/B against reference/shots/ffvi-battle-native-a.png at matched 768x672.

THE PIECE'S STATED PURPOSE IS ACHIEVED. The named failure -- a blurry or fractionally-scaled sprite -- does not occur. Canvas intrinsic 192x168 renders at exactly 384x336 CSS, scale 2.0000. At 400% browser zoom the scale becomes exactly 8. image-rendering: pixelated resolves last in all four stylesheets, so the crisp-edges ordering bug named in the brief is genuinely fixed.

I TESTED A BLUR HYPOTHESIS AND IT FAILED -- reporting it because it is the one thing that could have been an automatic loss. The stage sits at a fractional CSS offset: .cabinet is at top 135.5, so the canvas lands at top 143.5, which is 430.5 device px on a DPR-3 phone. I captured at DPR 3 and analysed the stage region for resampling. Result: 121 unique colours, ZERO with a channel that is not a multiple of 8, and 0.0% odd-length pixel runs in both axes. Chrome snaps the composited layer to the device grid, so nothing blurs. The half-pixel offset is a latent risk worth removing, not a live defect.

PALETTE ENGINEERING IS FLAWLESS AND SHOULD NOT BE TOUCHED. Decoded every one of the 33 atelier PNGs: 0 pixels off the 5-bit grid across the entire library. Every sprite is at or under 16 colours (slagmaw 15, heroes 11-14, items 3-7). Dither runs 0.0-3.1%, comfortably single-digit. ATB capsule is exactly 40x7 and heroes are exactly 16x24 idle / 24x32 attack, as specced. Only two assets exceed 16 colours -- scenes/slagfen.png at 29 and ui/window-band.png at 17 -- and both are backgrounds/chrome rather than sprites, which is legitimate under SNES subpalette rules.

THE CHROME BEATS THE BAR ON ITS OWN METRIC. Hue histogram of battle.html with the pixel stage excluded: only FOUR families above 0.15%, gold 7.72%, violet 1.04%, and the rest the cool near-black ground. reference/shots/ui-bar.png itself carries EIGHT families, gold 5.53%, violet 1.06%. We put 40% more gold on screen than the reference and fan across half as many hues. The gold serif title, the diamond-interrupted rule, the chamfered STRIKE plate and the currency chips are all reference-grade.

WHERE IT LOSES, BLIND: THE SPRITES. See progress/shots/battle-atelier-r1-critic-party-ours.png against -party-ffvi.png, identical crops at identical scale. FFVI's four heroes each hold a silhouette -- dark outline, interior folds, highlights on hair, tight elliptical contact shadows. Ours are a clump of flat colour blocks: the mage is a flat purple rectangle with one lighter stripe, the fourth hero is a featureless brown blob on two stick legs, and the cast shadows are oversized black smears that merge into one another.

FORMATION BUG, AND THE CODE KNOWS IT SHOULD NOT HAPPEN. src/js/screens/battle.js:71 comments 'party in a single file staggered down-right so nobody occludes anybody'. PARTY_SLOTS at line 74 steps x by 7 and y by 12 for sprites that are 16x24 -- that is 56% horizontal and 50% vertical overlap on every adjacent pair, and 71% horizontal during a 24x32 attack frame. The visible result is a gold shield prop sitting squarely over the next hero's head in every frame I captured. The comment and the numbers contradict each other.

DAMAGE NUMERALS COLLIDE, REPRODUCIBLY. Captured five frames across one encounter at 1.2s/3.0s/5.2s/7.4s/9.6s. When two numerals land on the same target they stack with insufficient separation and overlap illegibly -- '293' drawn through '370' in two separate frames. Single numerals (311, 168) are clean, so the defect is specifically the multi-hit vertical stagger.

BACKGROUND CRAFT TRAILS THE SPRITES. The horizon in slagfen.png is a strict alternating checker in a dead-straight line that reads as a tiling artifact rather than as dithered transition, the sky is a flat mauve gradient with sparse horizontal dashes standing in for clouds, and the skyline is flat black rectangles with yellow dots. FFVI's equivalent has genuine dithered cloud form, a value gradient into haze, and organically mottled ground with rocks of varied size.

NAMING IS CLEAN -- NO AUTOMATIC LOSS. Grepped src, tools and all root HTML for ~30 FFVI character, esper and place nouns. Zero hits in shipped strings; the only matches were substrings of 'unlocked'/'Locked'. All monster, hero, item and location names are invented.

REQUIRED FILES PRESERVED, WITH ONE INCONSISTENCY. src/assets/sprites/cog.png and aether-shard.png both decode as valid PNGs. However both are round-0 scaffold art and both are OFF the 5-bit grid (152 and 118 off-grid pixels respectively), so the two sprites actually visible in the shipped Skills tab violate the discipline the atelier page exists to certify.

THE ATELIER PAGE SLIGHTLY OVERCLAIMS. Its stat row reads '0 PX OFF-GRID / 15 COLOURS MAX / 3.7% DITHER MAX'. The first is exactly true and verified independently. '15 colours max' holds only if scenes and ui assets are excluded from the set the page says covers 'every sprite in Emberveil' -- slagfen.png is 29 and window-band.png is 17.

BLIND A/B RESULT: split. Shown the two stage crops with labels stripped, the FFVI capture is identifiable as the shipped product in about a second, and the tell is interior modelling -- its forms turn in light and ours are flat fills with outlines. Run the same test on the CHROME alone against ui-bar.png and ours wins. This piece is an excellent cabinet around art that is not yet finished, which is the exact inverse of the failure the brief was written to prevent.

CONTENT DEPTH, seconding the builder's own admission: three monsters, one scene, one region, a hardcoded two-enemy pair on a five-wave loop, and a finished 64x56 gloamstag that appears nowhere but the gallery. Real, but secondary to the modelling gap above -- more sprites at the current craft level would not close the distance to the bar.
